title: Subtraction games with at most three moves and the extension property have preperiod 0 (Miklós–Post Conjecture 2)

significance.root_decision: The conjecture holds: for a subtraction game with at most three moves and any seed, if p + x is an extension of the move set for every move x (p the period of the outcome sequence), then the outcome sequence is purely periodic. The source's extension criterion, applied at n + p, pulls the losing positions of the periodic tail backward into the start of the sequence; what remains is to exclude an extra early losing position. Such a position would force all of its forward neighbours to be winning in the periodic tail, and a new counting lemma (Lemma K: inclusion–exclusion on three translates of the set of losing residues, with matching singleton and pair counts and a pointwise triple inclusion) shows that this cannot happen when there are at most three moves. Lean proves the literal conjecture, the version with the hypothesis only for k = 1, a stronger pure-periodicity statement, and Lemma K; it also proves that the statement fails for four moves ({1,2,6,11}) and that Lemma K fails for {2,5,6,7}.
significance.caveat: The scope is that of Conjecture 2: binary win/loss outcomes, arbitrary seeds, at most three positive moves, and the extension hypothesis (the k = 1 hypothesis suffices; for seeded games it can hold when the all-k hypothesis fails). The argument is short and elementary; the contribution is the three-translate lemma. The source's separate remark that two-move games are purely periodic for arbitrary seeds is false under its printed recurrence, and its {3,5,11} example gives preperiod 11, not 12, under its own definition; neither affects Conjecture 2. No public resolution was found; exact-id omega registry queries on 2026-11-23 were rate-limited (keyword issue and pull-request queries returned nothing). Proof, first (same-model) review and Lean are by Claude Opus 5.5; the cross-model review and final check are by GPT-6.2 Sol (not routine 0.64).
